question: The Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulaha is located at ______
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah is located in **Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India**.
 
• It is also referred to as the **"Baby Taj"** due to its resemblance to the Taj Mahal and is considered a precursor to it.
 
• Built between **1622 and 1628** by Nur Jahan, the wife of Mughal Emperor Jahangir, in memory of her father, Mirza Ghiyas Beg.
 
• The tomb is the **first Mughal structure made entirely of white marble**, marking a departure from earlier Mughal architecture, which primarily used red sandstone.
 
• It is noted for its intricate **Pietra Dura (marble inlay) work** and is set in a **charbagh (four-part garden layout)**, a hallmark of Mughal design.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nur Jahan's architectural influence:**

 
 
• Nur Jahan was a powerful figure in Jahangir’s court and had a significant influence on Mughal architecture, including the design of this tomb.
 
• The tomb reflects Persian architectural elements, showcasing her Iranian heritage.
 
 
 
• **Pietra Dura technique:**
 
 
• Pietra Dura is a decorative art form involving inlaying semi-precious stones into marble, which became a key feature of Mughal architecture.
 
• The Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah is one of the earliest examples of this technique in India.
 
 
 
• **Charbagh layout:**
 
 
• The tomb is set within a charbagh, a Persian-inspired garden divided into four symmetrical parts by water channels.
 
• This layout symbolizes paradise in Islamic tradition.
 
 
 
• **Historical significance:**
 
 
• The Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah marks a transitional phase in Mughal architecture from massive red sandstone structures to elegant white marble buildings.
 
• It laid the foundation for later masterpieces like the Taj Mahal.
